name: Houzz

sources.title: Houzz Professionals directory — 'Join as a Pro' entry point; categories are all home design/remodeling/services trades

conditions: Pro profiles can be created via 'Join as a Pro', but the directory is gated to home design/remodeling/service professionals — a SaaS product does not qualify
The batch-provided pro-services/signUp URL 404s; the live entry point is the 'Join as a Pro' link on houzz.com/professionals
requirements: Business must be a home-industry professional: architects, interior designers, contractors, remodelers, landscapers, home services, etc. — categories on the directory are exclusively these trades
Requires a real business name, location/service area, phone/contact details and portfolio photos
Not applicable to pure software/SaaS products
preparation: Verify the product is actually a home-industry business (otherwise skip Houzz entirely)
Business name, address/service area, phone, website
Professional license info where applicable (Verified License badge exists)
workflow: Open houzz.com/professionals and click 'Join as a Pro'
Complete the pro registration with business category, location, and contact details
Build the profile with project photos, description, and services
Profile becomes discoverable in the Find Pros directory after review
watchFor: This is a wrong fit for SaaS — do not submit a software product; only a genuine home-services business belongs here
Houzz heavily upsells Houzz Pro (project management, CRM, payments) during onboarding
The sourced signup URL (pro-services/signUp) is dead; use the Join as a Pro flow from /professionals
countsAsLive: A public pro profile page appears in the Houzz professional directory under the chosen trade and metro area
unknowns: Exact fields/steps inside the Join as a Pro flow
Whether free-tier profiles still get full directory placement vs Houzz Pro subscribers
